images.title: Five jumps of 9.5
images.purpose: Show that 9.5 × 5 is 5 equal jumps of 9.5, and that the fraction route gives the same 47.5.
images.composition: One horizontal number line runs across the middle of the frame with 5 equal teal jumps above it; one short equation line sits centred below; white space above and below.
exact_structure: One horizontal grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 47.5, with exactly 6 labelled tick marks, equally spaced: 0, 9.5, 19, 28.5, 38, 47.5.
Exactly 5 equal curved teal #0072B2 jump arcs above the line, each from one labelled tick to the next.
The tick 47.5 and its label are in reddish purple #CC79A7.
Above the arcs, one teal #0072B2 caption "5 jumps of 9.5".
Below the line, one centred equation line in dark text #1F2937: "95/10 × 5 = 475/10 = 47.5".
No pens, no money symbols, no other ticks or numbers.
rejection: any number of jumps other than 5, or unequal jumps
any tick value other than 0, 9.5, 19, 28.5, 38 and 47.5
the equation showing any result other than 475/10 = 47.5
images.takeaway: Multiplying 9.5 by 5 by fractions gives the same 47.5 as adding 9.5 five times.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 47.5 with five equal jumps of 9.5 landing at 9.5, 19, 28.5, 38 and 47.5, above the equation 95/10 × 5 = 475/10 = 47.5.
images.context: Shown beside the pens worked example in the concept on a decimal times a number.
images.teaching_notes: Follow the jumps for the repeated addition, then read the equation to see the fraction route reach the same point.

image_decisions.why: A number line makes repeated addition visible and links it to the fraction product.
